lawyer:
Rafiqul Huq with Islam----------For respondent Nos. 2 and 3. 
Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Md. Shafiqur Rahman-----------For added respondent.
parties:
M. A. Sarnad------------Petitioner.
Vs.
The Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar North Comilla and others---------Respondents.
full_judgment:
Ruhul Islam C.J.—This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the action of the Sub- Divisional Officer Sadar (North), Comilla in abolishing Hasanpur S. N. College, P. S. Daudkandi, District Comilla by resolution dated 23rd September, 1975 as per annexure “C” to the petition should not be declared void, illegal and without lawful authority and why they should not be directed to supply Examination Entry Forms to Hasanpur S. N. College for H. S. C. Examination to be held in 1976 or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Petitioner's case, in short, is that he is the founder of Hasanpur S. N. College, under the Board of Intermediate & Secondary Education, Comilla, situated within P S. Dandkandi, District Comilla. The College was founded in the year 1948 as a full-fledged Intermediate College. It started functioning with sufficient number of students in 1st year Arts, Commerce and Science in the year 1969. The College was run by the organizing Committee headed by the petitioner as the Secretary of the said Organizing Committee. The petitioner and his brother donated 10.40 acres of land for the establishment of the college by a registered deed in 1969 and that he constructed a building measuring about 300 ft. in length for the college. Tin sheds were also constructed primarily for the accommodation of the college which was ultimately converted into a boarding house of the students after the main building of the college was constructed. The petitioner bore the entire expenses of the construction of the building and tin sheds. He also donated for purchasing science apparatus, books, furniture etc. His total contribution towards the establishment of Hasanpur S. N. College is more than Taka 10 lacs. The Sub-Divisional Officer Sadar (North) Comilla was the Ex-office Chairman of the Organising Committee of the College. Since 1970 onward number of students increased to about 600. With the provisional sanction of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla the examiners were sent up from Hasanpur S. N. College and that the Board granted affiliation to the College for a period of five years with effect from 1st July, 1969. After liberation of Bangladesh the petitioner was harassed by some interested group of people, and during that period an Ad-hoc Committee was formed for the management of the College in compliance of the order of the Government of Bangladesh. The sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (North) Comilla was made the Chairman of the Ad-hoc Committee. The College was granted affiliation by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education for a period of 5 (five) years with effect from 1st July, 1969. After 15th August, 1975 the Sub-Divisional Officer, under same outside influence, for amalgamating Hasanpur S. N, College and Munshi Fazlur Rahman College by abolishing the former convened a joint meeting of the Ad-hoc Committees of Hasanpur S. N. College and Munshi Fazlur Rahman College on 23rd September 1975 and persuaded the meeting to adopt a resolution unifying the two colleges into one college in the name and style Munshi Fazlur Rahman College to be run at the existing site of Munshi Fazlur Rahman College at Gouripur, The resolution further provided for removal of properties of Hasanpur S.N. College to the college site at Gouripur. 

 3. According to the petitioner the said illegal, void and unauthorised, because, neither the Sub-Divisional Officer nor the Ad-hoc Committees had the authority to amalgamate Hasanpur S. N. College and Munshi Fazlur Rahman College by abolishing the former. Further contention of the petitioner is that he, being the Founder and Donor of the College, the alleged resolution could not be passed in his absence without giving him any notice. When the petitioner learned about the alleged amalgamation he moved the appropriate authorities for restoring the college to its original position. The petitioner formed a new organizing Committee of which he is the Chairman. The petitioner submitted an application before the Inspector of Colleges. Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Comilla on 22nd July, 1976 along with a statement form duly filled in and deposited Taka 300/- being the affiliation fee for renewal extension of the affiliation of Hasanpur S. N. College, Hasanpur S. N. College with sound financial position has been functioning having about Taka 50,000/-in General Fund Account and Taka 10,000/-in Reserve Fund Account. The Inspector of Colleges by his letter dated 31st July, 1976 addressed to the Sub- Divisional officer asked his opinion as regards the proposal of Hasanpur S. N. College about sending up of examinees for the year 1976. The Inspector of Colleges also wrote letter dated 3rd April 1976 informing him that the petitioner claiming to be the founder of the college, submitted objection to the Chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla, to the unification of Hasanpur S. N. College with Munshi Fazlur Rahman College by abolishing the former. The Sub-Divisional Officer however, did not reply to the said letter. The petitioner then approached the Controller of Examinations for Entry Forms for about 200 examinees of Hasanpur S. N. College for the examination to be held in November/December, 1975 for the Session 1975-76 but the Controller of Examinations has not supplied the Examination Entry Forms. On these facts the petitioner moved the application for the relief as indicated above. 

 4. Respondent No 2 the Chairman. Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla and Respondent No. 3 the Controller of Examination of the Board entered appearance and have shown cause by filing an affidavit-in-opposition. In the affidavit the respondents admitted that affiliation to Hasanpur S. N. College was granted for a period of five years with effect from 1st July, 1969 in Humanities, Commerce and Science Groups imposing certain terms and conditions. As per terms and conditions provisional affiliation of the College expired on 30th June, 1974, and thereafter no formal prayer for extension was submitted before the Board by the said College till its amalgamation with Munshi Fazlur Rahman College. Respondents admitted that in pursuance of the Government's order dated 7th February, 1972 existing governing bodies were dissolved and were replaced by Ad-hoc committees in 1972. The Board received communication from the Government to the effect that the policy for amalgamation of adjacent colleges being under consideration of the Government, the Board was directed not to give further affiliation to any new college. The Board received a copy of the proceedings of the joint meeting of the governing bodies of the said two colleges held on 23rd September, 1976 containing the unanimous resolution to the effect that the two colleges were amalgamated with the name and style Munshi Fazlur Rahman College, Gouripur. The Board also received communication from the Sub-Divisional Officer that Hasanpur S.N. College and Munshi Fazlur Rahman College had been amalgamated into one College with the name and style of Munshi Fazlur Rahman College and that the Said Unification of the Colleges had been taken effect from 23rd September, 1975. According to the respondents Hasanpur S.N, College has not been enjoying affiliation since 1974 and it has been merged with Munshi Fazlur Ranman College. In this context the respondents further submitted that since the term of provisional affiliation of Hasaneur S.N. College expired on30th June, 1974 and no prayer for extension of the affiliation was submitted by the said College till its amalgamation with Munshi Fazlur Rahman College, the Beard was not in a position to consider the prayer for renewal of its affiliation specially in view of the directive of the Government prohibiting the Board from giving further affiliation to new colleges. 

 5. During the pendency of the Rule some members of the Government Body of the unified College filed an application for being added as respondents in the writ application. They were added as respondents 5-8. The added respondents filed an affidavit-in-opposition, wherein it has been stated, inter alia that the unification of the old Hasanpur College with the Gouripur Muhshi Fazlur Rahman College was accepted and recoenised by the authorities of the Chittagong University and the Beard of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Camilla It has been further stated that after unification or amalgamation of the two colleges there remained no existence of the old Hasanpur S.N. College in any form or manner and its affiliation granted by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla having expired in 1974 it was not renewed. The added respondents further slated that all the actions in the matter of unification of the Hasanpur S.N. College with Munshi Fazlur Rahman College, the latter of which is a degree college. is affiliated with the University of Chittagong, Munshi Fazlur Rahman College at Gouripur was started in 1966 as an Intermediate College and it was first affiliated to the Comilla Board with effect from 1970, and that degree classes were opened in this College from 1971-72 academic session, and college was affiliated as a Degree College with the University of Chittagong from 1971-72. Since, then the College has been enjoying such facilities till this day. College is governed by the Chittagong University Ordinance, 1966. In so far as constitution of its Governing Body of the College, Maintaining affiliation for Intermediate classes, controlling registration of students in Intermediate classes and holding examination of H.S.C. classes, the Comilla Board has no jurisdiction over the administration and Management of the College. The Gouripur Degree College is governed by the Regulations of the Chittagong University, copy of which was forwarded to the Munshi Fazlur Rahman College under their Memo: dated 19th September, 1976. On these facts the 'added respondents raised following points in resisting  the Rule : 

 (1) The Sub-Divisional Officer having acted as a member and Chairman of the Ad-hoc Governing Body of/Hasanpur S.N. College in all matters relating to the aforesaid unification, his acts are not acts as contemplated under Article 102 of the Constitution; and that unification of two colleges by the resolution dated 23rd September, 1975, being an act of two private non-government colleges is also not an act  as contemplated under Article 102 of the Constitution, and as such the application is not maintainable. 

 (2) The Sub-Divisional Officer having acted as Chairman of the Ad-hoc Governing Body of Hasanpur S.N. College, cannot be treated as a local authority within the meaning of Article 102 of the Constitution and as such the matter eject not come within the writ jurisdiction of this Court. 

 (3) The petitioner in his individual capacity as a donor or benefactor, has no locus standi to challenge the turn of unification without making the legal authorities of the concerned compete as party before the Court. 

 6. The question raised by the parties can be resolved on consideration of the following questions—(1) Whether the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (North) Comilla acted in his capacity as the Chairman of the Ad-hoc Committee of Hasanpur SN. College or in his officer capacity as the Sub.-Divisional Officer; (2) If the Sub-Divisional Officer acted in his officer capacity whether he had the authority to convene the joint meeting of the two Ad-hoc Committees end pass the impugned resolution; and (3) Whether the petitioner has locus standi to maintain the application. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits with reference to the Memo dated 17th September, 1975 ( Annexure '13') that the Sub-Divisional Officer convened the meeting of the Ad-hoc Committee of the respective Colleges in his official capacity which is also evident from the proceedings of the joint meeting itself held on 23rd September, 1975 (Annexure-3) copies of which were forwarded to the (1), Secretary, Ministry of Education, Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh, Dacca (2) Director, Public Instruction, Bangladesh, Dacca, (3) The Deputy Commissioner, Comilia, (4) Inspector of Colleges, University of Chittagong, (5) Chairman, Board of intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla, (6) Controller of Examination; Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla, (7) Inspector of Colleges, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education; Comilla, etc. The learned Advocate further submits with reference to the Bangladesh Committee of Management (Temporary Arrangement) Order, 1977 (President’s) order No. 117 of 1972) that Ad-hoe Committee of the respective colleges was appointed under the direction from the Government as temporary .arrangement to provide for consideration of certain Committees of management with a view to provide proper functioning of the institutions ; and that the Ad-hoc Committees were appointed "to run the day to-day affairs of the institution". They had no authority to dissolve the institution or merge the institution with any other institution. In this connection the learned Advocate further submits that the petitioner's case is that Sub-Divisional Officer under some extraneous influence convened the joint meeting of the Ad-hoc Committees and managed to get the re-solution passed without at all taking into consideration the interest of the Hasanpur S.N. College and the education of its students. The learned Advocate also submits that the petitioner being the founder and donor of the institution was entitled to a notice of the meeting as provided under the regulations and the Sub-Divisional Officer also acknowledging the right of the founder and donor gave direction in his order on conditions laid down in the letter dated 2nd March, 1974 (Annexure A) granting affiliation for five years with effect from 1st July, 1969. The college suffers from no financial difficulties which is indicated from the certificate from the relevant Banks. Annexures F and G to the application show that the college maintain General Fund Accounts with the Janata Bank, Comilla (Main) Branch having balance in thee account as on 29th July, 1976 in Taka 50,000/- and the college maintains Reserve Fund Account in the same Bank with a balance in Taka 10,000/-. In this context the learned Advocate also refers to a letter of the Principal in-charge of Hasanpur S.N. College dated 26th July, 1976 addressed to Controller of Examination, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla reporting probable number of H.S.C. candidates for the year 1976 in Science 75, in Commerce 50, and in Humanities 75. In this letter the Principal requested the authority to supply 200 H.S.C. Examination Entry Forms along with other relevant papers to that the College could send up H.S.C. Candidates for 1976. The question of recognition of Hasanpur S N. College as a separate entry an extension of its affiliation was under the active consideration of the Board, as indicated from the letter: dated 3rd April. 1976 and 31st July, 1976 from the Inspector of Colleges to the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (North), Comilla asking his views Finally, the learned Advocate submits that in the absence of a proper legislation by the Government the college could not be merged with another college by abolishing it, and as such the action being entirely illegal and without any lawful authority the impugned resolution cannot be sustained, and the college, should be allowed to continue functioning independently. 

 8. It is not disputed that the petitioner A. Samad is the founder, of Hasanpur S.N College also not disputed that he donated quite a substantial quantity of land, that is, 10.40 acres and that he spent several lacs of takas towards construction of the building, purchasing apparatus, books and furniture etc. From the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Constitution, Powers and Duties of Government Bodies of Non-Government Intermediate College) Regulations, 1975, it appears that status of a founder of a college has been given a definite status. Regulation 2(d) reads as Under: 

 Regulation 4 provides Constitution of Governing Bodies. Sub clause (iii) of clause (d) provides that two representatives of the founders, trustees, benefactors and donors from amongst themselves. Regulation 5(2) provides that a founder shall be a voter for his life time. Direction of the Sub-Divisional Officer to serve notice upon the founder was in consonance with the provisions of the Regulations that the petitioner is a benefactor or the college and he made sufficient contribution towards the college; and that he is still actively looking after the college is not seriously disputed. Apart from the right of a founder as conferred under the Regulations, we have no doubt that the petitioner in his capacity of the founder and donor of the Hasanpur S.N. College has got the right to protect it, from any sort of invasion for destroying or adversely affecting it as a separate entity. The petitioner has got the vested right to participate in any arrangement that might affect the interest of the College. Therefore, we have no doubt that the petitioner in his capacity as the founder of the college is .entitled to be treated as an aggrieved person within, the meaning of Article 102 of the Constitution, and as such he has locus standi to maintain the application. 

 9. The Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (North) Comilla cannot be said to have acted in his private capacity as contended by the added respondent. Even if it is accepted that the Sub-Divisional Officer acted merely as the ex-office Chairman of the Ad hoc Committee of Hasanpur S.N. College his function as such cannot be treated .to be in his private capacity, because, he was appointed as the ex-office Chairman of the College when the Ad-hoc Committee was constituted under the provisions of President's Order No. 117 of 1972, that is to say, an authority constituted and functioning under a statute. However, it is clear to us that the Sub-Divisional Officer did not act merely in his capacity as the Chairman of the Ad-hoc Committee but in his capacity as the Sub-Divisional Officer. The order of the Sub Divisional Officer dated 17th September, 1975 Governing joint meeting of the two Ad-hoc Committees (Annexure B), does not show that the order was passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer in his capacity as the Chairman of the Ad-hoc Committee Hasanpur S.N. College. That the Sub-Divisional Officer did not act in his private capacity is also indicative from other papers referred to above. Therefore; the action of the Sub-Divisional Officer in convening the joint meeting of the two Ad-hoc Committees and the resolution adopted in the joint meeting held on 23rd September, 1975 are actions which can be challenged under a tide 102 of the Constitution. 

 10. The Sub-Divisional Officer has not entered appearance in this matter, although notice of the Rule Nisi was duly served upon him. Nothing has been produced before us So show that the Sub-Divisional Officer or for that matter the Ad-hoc Committee of Hasanpur S. N. College had the authority to take the impugned decision of unification of the two colleges by abolishing Hasanpur S.N. College altogether and merging the same With the Muhshi Fazlur Rahman College. It has been already indicated above that the Ad-hoc Committee of the respective college was constituted under the President's Order No. 117 of 1972 only for some limited purpose and for a limited period. Annexures E and F, that is, two Memorandums dated 25th May 1972 and 30th May, 1972, are the reports from the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Comilla to the Inspector of Colleges; Beard of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Comilla which show that the Ad-hoc Committees had been constituted with the personnel as stated therein "to run the day to day affairs of the Colleges." Ad-hoc Committees so constituted could not take such a vital decision. Besides the joint meeting was held without giving any notice to the founder of Hasanpur S. N. College, .although the Sub-Divisional Officer gave direction to that effect. 

 1. It is unanimously resolved that both Munshi Fazlur Rahman College and Hasanpur S. N. College be unified into one college in the name and style Munshi Fazlur Rahman College and be run in the existing site of Munshi Fazlur Rahman College at Gouripur in the greater interest of the people of the elaka and for better educational facilities and to meet the needs of higher education of rural people. 

 3. It is further resolved that Mr. Akhtar Alam Khan, Deputy Magistrate. Sadar (North) Comilla be requested to take over all assets including all other movable and immovable properties of Hasanpur S. N. College and subsequently make over the same to the Principal of M. F. College as per list furnished by the Principal of Hasanpur S. N. College. Principal of Hasanpur S. N. College Will make over all assets (both Moveable and immovable properties) to the above Deputy Magistrate. 

 12. There is no doubt that the joint meeting of the Ad-hoc Committee decided to completely dissolve Hasanpur S. N. College and its movable properties to be taken over by Munshi Fazlur Rahman. College although the Ad-hoc Committee had riot the authority to take any such action. The learned Advocates appearing for respondents 2 and 3 and the added respondents could not place before us any authority to support the said re-solution. It has been indicated above that the Sub-Divisional Officer convened the joint meeting of the two Ad-hoc Committees without any lawful authority. Therefore, the joint meeting held on the 23rd September, 1975 was not validly held and consequently the resolution of unification of the two colleges adopted in the joint meeting is wholly illegal and without any lawful authority. By such an illegal action a college which was running independently, and for all practical purposes satisfactorily under the direct Control of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, could not be abolished or merged with any other institution, in the manner as stated above. 

 13. We do not find any substance in the contention of the added respondents that the resolution dated 23rd September, 1975 having already been acted upon by the relevant authorities the arrangement of unification of the two colleges cannot be interfered with in exercising the power of this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution. If the resolution of so-called unification or merger is found wholly illegal and without any lawful authority, the factum of giving effect to the said resolution cannot stand in 'the way of granting an appropriate relief as found necessary. Apart from that, such objection has not been raised by respondents 2 and 3. But on the other hand, Annexure 'E' to the application, receipt dated 22nd July, 1976 granted by the Accounts Assistant of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary. Education, Comilla shows that the Principal of Hasanpur S.N. College sent a requisite to the Board for 250 H.S.C. Entry Forms and supplied the number of H.S.C. candidates for 1976; his Science 75; in Commerce 50; and in Humanities Annexure 'T' and show that the 'prayer of the College for renewal of affiliation of the college as a separate entity was under active consideration of the Board, and the petitioner rightly contends that affiliation would have been extended but for the directive from the government not to give affiliation to a new college (Annexure to the affidavit-in-opposition of respondents 2 and 3) because, Hasanpur S.N. College is not a newly established college. 

 14. In the circumstances stated above, the application must succeed. The second part of the Rule Nisi, namely, relating to prayer for direction upon the respondents 2 and 3 for supplying Examination Entry Forms to Hasanpur S.N. College for the H.S.C. Examination to be held in 1976, having become infructuous on account of the examination for the year 1976 having already been held, the prayer is not pressed and, as such, no direction is necessary. The Rule Nisi excepting the second party as indicated above,  is made absolute, It is declared that the action of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (North), Comilla in abolishing Hasanpur S.N. College, P.S. Daudkandi, District Comilla by the resolution dated the 23rd September, 1975 is illegal and without any lawful authority.
